title: Fix deprecated --no-highlight and --highlight-style flags for Pandoc >= 3.8
description:
When rendering with Pandoc >= 3.8, `html_document_clean()` always emits a deprecation warning because Pandoc 3.8 deprecated `--no-highlight` and `--highlight-style` in favor of `--syntax-highlighting`. This breaks rmarkdown's daily CI check against Pandoc nightly, which renders a document using `cleanrmd::html_document_clean()` with Pandoc warnings treated as errors (rstudio/rmarkdown#2640):

```
Error: Pandoc reported warning(s):
  Deprecated: --no-highlight. Use --syntax-highlighting=none instead.
```

The internal `pandoc_html_highlight_args()` hardcoded the deprecated flags on every code path: `highlight = NULL`, prism themes (`--no-highlight` + `--variable use-prism=...`), and named styles (`--highlight-style`).

This applies the same fix as rstudio/rmarkdown#2602 in rmarkdown's own `pandoc_highlight_args()`: with Pandoc >= 3.8 it emits `--syntax-highlighting none` / `--syntax-highlighting <style>`, and keeps the old flags for older Pandoc. Prism theme handling, the `arrow`/`rstudio` theme file resolution, and the `highlight = "default"` to `"arrow"` mapping are unchanged.

The existing tests were made version-conditional, and rendering was verified end-to-end:

- Pandoc 3.11: `highlight: prism`, `highlight: NULL`, `highlight: tango`, and `highlight: default` all render without any `Deprecated:` warning; prism CSS link present for prism, no highlighting CSS for `NULL`, Pandoc highlighting CSS present for tango and default.
- Pandoc 3.1.13 (via `pandoc::with_pandoc_version()`): the legacy `--no-highlight` / `--highlight-style` flags are still used and all four documents render correctly.

title: Add five new themes and center document body in the template
description:
Fixes #12
Fixes #15
Fixes #17
Adds themes from #22

## Summary

**Five new classless themes (30 → 35):**

| Theme | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `basic.css` | Vladimir Carrer | Classless starter file, stable/frozen upstream (#15) |
| `bolt.css` | Ty Bolt | Minified build; built-in light/dark modes (#22) |
| `classlesscss` | Emanuel Regnath | classless.css v1.1 (#17) |
| `mvp.css` | Andy Brewer | MVP.css v1.18 (#12) |
| `neat.css` | Joel Dare | Auto light/dark via `color-scheme` (#22) |

Each author is credited in `DESCRIPTION` and each theme's MIT license is recorded in `inst/resources/NOTICE`. Updated `R/sysdata.rda`, roxygen docs, and README.

**Template centering fix:** the cleanrmd template now applies `html body { margin-inline: auto }` *after* the theme stylesheet. Themes that reset the body margins without providing their own width container (`bullframe`, `mvp`) were pinning the template's 48em content column to the left edge of the viewport. The higher-specificity `html body` selector is required because the theme picker injects theme styles at the end of `<head>`.

**DoodleCSS** (also suggested in #22) was skipped: it requires `class="doodle"` on `<body>` plus a Google Fonts import, conflicting with cleanrmd's bare-HTML promise. attriCSS (#10) was evaluated and left out to keep the bundled set lean.

## Verification

- `testthat::test_local()`: 42 pass, 0 fail
- R CMD check locally: 0 errors, 0 warnings
- All vendored files verified as genuine CSS after download
- Template fix verified in both fixed-theme and theme-picker modes via a rendered docs page
- Preview with `cleanrmd::use_cleanrmd()` and pick a new theme from the picker

title: Refresh themes: bullframe v6, water auto, bundle updates, picker persistence
description:
Closes #40
Closes #33
Closes #31

## Summary

- **bullframe v6 (#40):** bump to the v6 classless build via the bullframe.css CDN (vendored copy was v4.0.1 from `master`).
- **water auto (#33):** the `water` theme now uses water.css's automatic stylesheet, which follows the reader's `prefers-color-scheme`. `water-dark` is unchanged for readers who want an always-dark theme.
- **Theme picker persistence (#31):** the picker stores the reader's last selected theme in `localStorage` and restores it on return visits, falling back to the default theme when nothing is stored or the stored theme no longer exists. Storage access is wrapped in try/catch for private/sandboxed browsing contexts.
- **Author-settable default theme (#31):** `use_cleanrmd()` and `cleanrmd_theme_dependency()` gain a `default` argument (default: `"new.css"`) used by the theme picker until the reader picks a theme.
- **Bundle refresh:** re-ran `data-raw/gather-css.R` to update all themes pinned to moving URLs (axist, bamboo, holiday, latex.css with refreshed fonts, marx, picocss, sakura, sakura-vader, simplecss).
- **vanilla URL fix:** `vanillacss.com` now redirects to an unrelated site (a refresh briefly vendored a spam HTML page as `vanilla.css`), so the theme now downloads from `bradleytaunt/vanilla-css` on GitHub. Content is unchanged from the previously vendored version.
- Also fixes the `new.css` download URL (`master` → `main`), which prevented `gather-css.R` from completing.

## Verification

- `testthat::test_local()`: 42 pass, 0 fail (5 new tests for the picker JSON and `default` argument)
- Theme picker JS smoke-tested with a DOM stub (9 scenarios incl. localStorage-denied fallback)
- Preview with: `cleanrmd::use_cleanrmd()` in an R Markdown document, pick a theme, reload, and confirm the selection is restored

title: Fixes the behavior of the title_in_header
description: After a lot of confusion, and not managing to get the `title_in_header` working, I realized that maybe the implementation is not correct. This tiny patch fixes the issue for me, and I can use the `title_in_header: false` and not get the title as a header in the HTML! 🙂

title: Add `use_cleanrmd()`
description: Fixes #26 by exporting `use_cleanrmd()` and its lower-level counterpart `cleanrmd_theme_dependency()`, making it possible to use cleanrmd themes in a variety of places. The descriptions below are taken from the new `?use_cleanrmd()` docs. ### R Markdown documents In R Markdown (static or Shiny prerendered), you should use the `html_document_clean()` output format to use a cleanrmd theme. --- output: cleanrmd::html_document_clean: theme: NULL # or pick a specific theme self_contained: false --- ### Quarto documents You can also use cleanrmd in Quarto documents or apps (using `server: shiny`). You'll need to turn off the themes provided by Quarto with `theme: none` and then call `cleanrmd::use_cleanrmd()` in a code chunk in your document. --- title: "Untitled" format: html: theme: none #server: shiny --- ```{r cleanrmd, echo=FALSE} cleanrmd::use_cleanrmd("bamboo") ``` ### Shiny apps In Shiny apps, you'll need to use `shiny::basicPage()` rather than `shiny::fluidPage()`. Then call `use_cleanrmd()` in your app and you'll use a clean theme. library(shiny) ui <- shiny::basicPage( cleanrmd::use_cleanrmd(), h2("Old Faithful Geyser Data"), sliderInput( "bins", "Number of bins:", min = 1, max = 50, value = 30 ), plotOutput("distPlot") )
